evidence.decision: Separates transient focus, deliberate activation and persistent selection, deciding when an initial focus is harmless and when automatic movement would change context.
evidence.artifact: Delivers a focus-group/order map and separate visual states, including removal/return behavior that can be implemented or tested through navigation paths.
evidence.transformation: The TV watchlist example stops autoplay on focus and replaces an ambiguous saved glow with separate focus, Select activation and persistent Saved state.
evidence.verification: Checks directional entry, removal and return for traps, jumps and lost selected state, without equating a static map with actual focus-engine or hardware execution.
evidence.applicability: Keeps TV directional navigation and five states distinct from iPad Tab/arrow grouping and Full Keyboard Access; does not generalize this component guidance to iOS/watchOS or equate gaze hover with focus.
evidence.handoffs: Uses Remotes for TV button semantics, Keyboards for access routes and Eyes for spatial hover rather than folding their different semantics into focus.
evidence.distinctiveness: Focus-versus-selection state separation, one-step replacement after removal, visible-content gestures and platform navigation grouping give this procedure a concrete interaction model.
